label: Someone has been in error about a moral…, from Moral judgments have a truth value: in… and 1 more
meaning: Q-MORAL-ERROR, Catholic cell (ST I-II q.94 a.4). Moral judgments have a truth value, and the Germans held one that is not true (robbery is not unjust), so they erred about a moral matter. The countermodel withoutTruthAptnessNoError shows truth-aptness is needed: without it the same belief is no error, which is exactly emotivism's position. Q-MORAL-PROGRESS: the Catholic answer is the correction of such corruption (claim AQUINAS-ST-I-II-Q94-A5-AD1-CORRECTION). Its two premises are sourced but undefended: the Germans' judgment being untrue rests on the natural law, which this result does not prove.
